headline: BOC, BIR Flag Funding Gaps in Fight Against Cigarette Smuggling
seoTitle: BOC, BIR Flag Anti-Smuggling Funding Gaps | FMB News
seoDescription: Customs and tax authorities told lawmakers that funding and equipment gaps are limiting enforcement against illicit cigarette smuggling in the Philippines.
deck: Finance officials told a House hearing that Customs needs more resources for maritime assets, compulsory acquisition and legal support as illicit tobacco enforcement intensifies.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Bureau of Customs and Bureau of Internal Revenue have flagged resource shortages affecting the government's campaign against cigarette smuggling, according to the Department of Finance during a House Ways and Means Committee hearing on August 25.

DOF Fiscal Policy and Monitoring Undersecretary Karlo Fermin Adriano said the agencies submitted reports detailing enforcement needs after lawmakers asked what additional support would strengthen the campaign.

sections.heading: Where the gaps are
paragraphs: Among the Customs concerns cited at the hearing were insufficient funding to use compulsory-acquisition provisions against undervalued shipments, inadequate resources to acquire land, air and water assets for anti-smuggling operations, and a lack of legal support for personnel testifying in smuggling cases.
The funding discussion comes amid a broader government drive against illicit tobacco, including recent large-scale seizures and tighter controls over confiscated cigarette inventories.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: In June, a joint BOC, NBI, BIR and Philippine Coast Guard operation intercepted 23 containers of illicit cigarettes valued at about P1.7 billion. Customs has also ordered stronger security and accountability measures for confiscated cigarettes held at ports nationwide.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Illicit cigarette trade can reduce tax collections, undercut lawful businesses and expose enforcement personnel to well-funded smuggling networks. Budget support matters only if it produces accountable equipment, stronger case preparation and measurable enforcement results.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Lawmakers are expected to weigh the agencies' operational requirements during budget deliberations. The key question is whether additional 2027 appropriations translate into more maritime enforcement capacity, testing capability and legal support for frontline personnel.
